title: Saskatchewan Corporate Registry Search (ISC Guide)
h1: How to Search the Saskatchewan Corporate Registry (ISC)
description: How to search Saskatchewan's Corporate Registry: ISC's application, free no-login options, what records show, and fees for reports and certificates.
body:
**Need the full picture on a Saskatchewan company?** [Order a corporate profile report — {{price:profile-report}} + GST, delivered within 1 business hour →](/order/profile-report?src=article-saskatchewan-corporate-registry-search) · Directors, registered office, status and filing history, pulled directly from the registry.

Saskatchewan does its corporate registry differently. In most provinces the registry is a government office; in Saskatchewan it's operated by **ISC — Information Services Corporation** — a publicly traded company that runs the province's land titles, personal property and corporate registries under agreement with the Government of Saskatchewan. The public face is **Saskatchewan Registry Services** at saskregistries.ca, and the actual database — where you search for a company, pull its record or file against it — is the **Corporate Registry application** at corporateregistry.isc.ca. This guide covers how to search it, the free no-login alternatives, what a Saskatchewan record shows, and what ISC charges for reports and certificates.

## Where Do You Search the Saskatchewan Corporate Registry?

The official route is ISC's Corporate Registry application. You can search by **business (entity) name or entity number**, and the application holds entity information from **1999 to the present** — anything earlier has to be requested from ISC through its document order form rather than found onscreen.

The catch is the login. ISC's own search guidance directs you to **log in to the Corporate Registry application to search**, and the Corporate Registry application takes its own account — separate, confusingly, from the account used for ISC's other online services like land titles. If you only need to confirm that one company exists before signing a contract, creating a registry account is a lot of setup for a single name lookup.

That's the trade-off to understand up front: ISC's application is the authoritative source and the only place to order Saskatchewan's official documents directly, but it's built for people who interact with the registry regularly — law firms, accountants, search houses — not for a one-time check.

## Can You Search a Saskatchewan Company Without an ISC Account?

Yes. Two free routes return Saskatchewan corporations with no registry login:

1. **Canada's Business Registries search** — the federal aggregator run by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada includes Saskatchewan alongside the other participating provincial registries. Type a name or business number and Saskatchewan entities come back with their status and jurisdiction, no account needed.
2. **[CRS's Canada corporations search](/canada-corporations-search)** — searches Saskatchewan and the other Canadian registries from one box, free and without a login, and shows the company's name, status and registry details on the spot. If the free result isn't enough, you can order the official record from the same page.

For how Saskatchewan fits into the national picture — which registries exist, what each is called, and which companies show up where — see our guide to [searching Canadian business registries](/articles/how-to-search-canadian-business-registries).

One scope note: the free aggregator routes are built around registered corporations and business names. Pre-1999 history, filed documents and certified copies still only come from ISC itself — or from a registry agent who orders them for you.

## What Does a Saskatchewan Corporate Registry Search Show?

A basic search result confirms the entity exists and gives you its registry identity — the exact legal name, entity number, entity type and current status. The full public record behind it is what ISC sells as a **corporate registry profile report**, and it includes the entity type and status, the registration or incorporation date, the nature of business, the registered office and mailing address, the owners and directors on file, and the entity's event history — name changes, amalgamations and the like.

Two details worth reading closely:

- **Status: Active vs Struck.** An active corporation is on the register and in good order. Saskatchewan's registrar can strike a corporation that stops filing its annual returns, and a struck company has no legal capacity to carry on business until it's revived. If a company you're about to pay shows as struck or dissolved, stop and ask questions before money moves. (If the struck company is yours, the fix starts with the overdue filings — our guide to the [Saskatchewan annual return](/articles/how-to-file-your-annual-return-in-saskatchewan) covers the deadline and the $60 government fee, which jumps to $110 once you're late.)
- **What's *not* in the public record.** Shareholdings are not part of the registry's public file — share registers live with the corporation's own records. The profile report shows directors and officers, which is usually what a bank, landlord or lawyer actually wants to verify.

## What Do ISC Registry Documents and Certificates Cost?

ISC publishes a consolidated Corporate Registry fee table; the figures below are from the schedule in effect since **April 15, 2026**. These are the government-side fees you pay ISC directly through the Corporate Registry application:

| Item | ISC fee |
|---|---|
| Profile report | $10 |
| Certificate of Status | $15 |
| Copies of filed documents | $12 per document |
| Electronic certification | $5 per document |
| Manual certification | $40 per document |
| Priority service on a document order | $75 per order |
| Name search and reservation (for-profit) | $50 |

The fee table has no line item for the basic search itself — what you pay for are the documents. The practical cost of going direct is the account setup and portal navigation, which is exactly what a registry agent removes: CRS pulls the official Saskatchewan record with no ISC account on your end — a [corporate profile report](/order/profile-report?src=article-saskatchewan-corporate-registry-search) for {{price:profile-report}} + GST within 1 business hour, or a [certificate of good standing](/order/good-standing?src=article-saskatchewan-corporate-registry-search) for {{price:good-standing}} all-in + tax. For what the certificate proves and when you need one, see our walkthrough on [getting a certificate of good standing in Saskatchewan](/articles/how-to-get-a-certificate-of-good-standing-in-saskatchewan).

## How Do You Verify a Saskatchewan Company Before You Do Business With It?

Run the name through a free search first — Canada's Business Registries or [CRS's registry search](/canada-corporations-search) — and check three things: the status is active, the legal name matches the name on your contract or invoice exactly, and the incorporation date is consistent with how long the company claims to have operated. A name that returns nothing may be a federal corporation, a company registered in another province, or an unregistered trade name — and sometimes a business that simply doesn't exist. Our guide to [verifying a Canadian company](/guides/how-to-verify-a-canadian-company) covers the red flags once the record is in hand.

For anything with real stakes — a supplier contract, a lease, litigation, buying the company — get the official record rather than relying on a free summary. A profile report shows the directors, addresses and event history on the registry's file; a Certificate of Status proves the company is active as of the date issued.

And if your search is the first step toward starting your own company rather than checking someone else's, our guide to [incorporating in Saskatchewan](/articles/how-to-incorporate-in-saskatchewan) breaks down every fee, from the $255 government incorporation charge to the $50 name reservation.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is searching the Saskatchewan Corporate Registry free?

ISC's fee schedule doesn't charge for the basic lookup — you pay for documents, like the $10 profile report or $15 Certificate of Status. But ISC's guidance directs you to log in to the Corporate Registry application to search, so going direct means creating a registry account first. Canada's Business Registries and CRS's Canada corporations search are free with no login.

### What is ISC in Saskatchewan?

ISC (Information Services Corporation) is the publicly traded company that operates Saskatchewan's registries — corporate, land titles and personal property — under agreement with the provincial government. For corporate searches and filings, its public site is Saskatchewan Registry Services (saskregistries.ca) and the database itself is the Corporate Registry application at corporateregistry.isc.ca.

### How do I find out if a Saskatchewan company is still active?

Search the name in Canada's Business Registries or CRS's Canada corporations search and read the status. Active means the company is on the register; struck or dissolved means it has lost its status — often for unfiled annual returns — and can't legally carry on business until revived. For formal proof, order a Certificate of Status from ISC or a certificate of good standing through CRS for {{price:good-standing}} all-in + tax.

### How much is a Saskatchewan corporate profile report?

ISC charges $10 for a profile report ordered through its Corporate Registry application, which requires an ISC registry account. CRS retrieves the same official record for {{price:profile-report}} + GST with no account setup on your end, delivered as a PDF within 1 business hour.

### Can I see who owns a Saskatchewan company?

Not through the registry's public record — shareholder details live in the corporation's own share register, not on ISC's public file. The profile report does show the directors, officers, registered office and event history, which covers most due-diligence needs. For ownership, you have to ask the company itself.

## Search Done — Now Get the Document

A free search tells you a Saskatchewan company exists. When a bank, lawyer or counterparty wants proof, CRS pulls the official record with no ISC account and no portal navigation: a [corporate profile report](/order/profile-report?src=article-saskatchewan-corporate-registry-search) for {{price:profile-report}} + GST within **1 business hour**, a [certificate of good standing](/order/good-standing?src=article-saskatchewan-corporate-registry-search) for {{price:good-standing}} all-in + tax, or a [full corporate search](/order/corporate-search?src=article-saskatchewan-corporate-registry-search) for {{price:corporate-search}} + tax when you need the complete document set.

**Turnaround:** profile reports within 1 business hour; certificates within 3 business hours.
